rows.title: Getting Around › Flying the universe
rows.text: The whole cosmos is one continuous view. Pinch or scroll to zoom, drag to pan. Zooming dives through four scales: universe → galaxy → star system → planet surface — and zooming out climbs back up. Everything you can see, you can visit. Tap any object to open its survey card ; tap it again (or tap elsewhere) to release. When a planet fills the view but sits off-center, keep zooming — the camera glides the rest of the way in. On a world you’ve never stood on, the dive stops at approach altitude and asks before you commit — see Landing . Panning and pinching are never hijacked. On a surface, you walk the world itself — the survey card stays pinned. Travel beyond your charted frontier is gated — see Frontier regions .

rows.title: Getting Around › Survey cards
rows.text: Knowing a world comes in three acts. Glance : on a computer, hovering shows the long-range reads — color class, atmosphere, water signatures, whispers of life (on a phone your tap goes straight to the survey). Orbital survey : tap to lock the card and the instruments speak — environment, biosphere, signals. Ground survey : land — press the card’s Land button, or dive toward the world and confirm the descent (see Landing ); planetfall opens the census of any civilization and the mineral veins of dead worlds. Every line is generated from the object’s seed, so your survey matches every other explorer’s. Tapping locks the card in place so you can press its buttons while the object drifts. A planet’s card leads with its actions and headlines; the Environment row’s expand pill unfolds the full readings, and a civilization’s headline unfolds its census. Cards remember whether you like them open or folded — the ⟁ Signal row never hides, and a world you’ve stood on wears a Ground-surveyed tag. An organized world announces itself from orbit as ⟁ signals — land to attempt first contact . Most receptions are warm; a wary one wounds you (a named Field Scout takes the hit instead), and the census stays sealed until a landing goes well. Conquest never needs to ask. Worlds with a biosphere show Discover Life — see Discovering life . The bookmark row saves the place — see The Star Atlas . Every planet’s card names its biome — swamp world, carbon world, magma sea — and the rare kinds announce themselves in violet. A glance that whispers impossible biosignatures means something is alive where nothing should be. Worlds of renown (v1.7): the rarest worlds carry an epithet — the Shrouded , the Ringed Court — the same name for every explorer, forever. Rare near home; commoner in the deep field. Stand on a world and its mineral veins show their grade for that ground (Primordial worlds enrich every seam one step), and an ⬆ Leave this world button pulls the camera back to the system overview.

rows.title: Getting Around › Landing
rows.text: Setting down is the one moment the frontier pushes back. Every world sits somewhere on a ladder, from a calm approach that always works to a hostile dive that mostly doesn’t — the odds come from what the world is, and a storm blowing right now shaves a little more off. You see the number before you commit. Zooming into an unvisited world stops at approach altitude and asks. The Land button on a survey card skips the question — pressing it is the answer. A failed descent is a wave-off: you’re bounced back to orbit with a scrape, never worse. It cannot kill you. Every wave-off teaches the approach — your next try on that world is a fair bit better, and the lesson is remembered even between sessions. Once you’ve stood on a world it is yours: return landings always succeed, no questions asked. Earth is home. Home never waves you off.

rows.title: Getting Around › Search
rows.text: The search box (top bar) hunts across everything you’ve already discovered: Atlas places and Compendium species. It also accepts pasted codes: CF1-… world codes — jump straight to a friend’s discovery. CFB-… creature codes — load a friend’s creature for a duel. Worlds bookmark under their biome — searching swamp or carbon finds every one you’ve saved since v1.3.5. See Share codes .

rows.title: Getting Around › Share codes (CF1 / CFB)
rows.text: There is no server — the universe is mathematics, identical on every device. A share code is just an address into that shared math: ⇪ Share this discovery on a survey card copies a CF1- code/link. Anyone who opens it lands on the exact same world, with your name for it attached. ⇪ Code on a creature card copies a CFB- code carrying the full genome — the identical creature, stats and all, appears on your friend’s device for a duel. Codes are sanitized on arrival; a tampered code can’t hurt your save.

rows.title: Getting Around › Expedition Charters
rows.text: The Charters board (the 📜 pill — left rail on desktop, dock on phones) always has work for an explorer. Charters arrive in chains that reveal one link at a time: the five trades (planetfall, prospecting, discovering life, naming a Field Scout, conquest) and the Sol tour , a guided lap of the home system that pays its way in starter gear. Completing a link reveals the next — and a link your ring can’t reach yet stays off the board until the sky opens. Accept to begin. A revealed charter tracks nothing until you press Accept — three may ride at once. Accept a deed the frontier has already seen you do and it completes on the spot, already proven ; counting charters count from the accept and say so. Each pays ☄ Stardust — some pay gear — the moment it completes. Once the five trades are learned, the board turns weekly: three charters a week, identical for every explorer in the universe — deterministic, like everything else out here. Compare boards with a friend; they match. The objective chip (v1.7): the pill under the dock is a live tracker — your accepted charter first, otherwise the chapter’s next goal, with running progress that pulses when it moves. Tap it for the board. The pinned Ascent chapter above the charters is your mainline story: no accepting needed, it is always yours.

rows.title: Getting Around › Traveler’s Beacon
rows.text: The Traveler’s Beacon (left rail) offers a fresh destination every 5 minutes — always somewhere inside your charter : it walks Sol while Sol is your world, the Neighborhood once you can jump, the whole galaxy once the Array is up, and the wider cosmos beyond the Rim. Picked deterministically, so every explorer on your ring is pointed at the same place at the same moment. An easy way to see something new when the infinite feels too big.

rows.title: Getting Around › The Star Atlas
rows.text: Your personal map of the infinite. On any survey card: + Add to Star Atlas bookmarks the place. ☆ Favorite marks your best finds (and auto-saves them). ⌂ Home marks one place as home — yours to change anytime. The weekly pool now includes Down the hard way — land on a gas giant, a hothouse or a molten world. The descent will fight you; that’s the point. Open the Star Atlas (the dock — or the right rail on desktop) and tap any entry to ride the hyperlane there — the camera dives out, the sky stretches into a streak tunnel tinted by your destination’s light, and you ease in on arrival (tap to skip; obeys your effects and Motion settings). The Atlas keeps your most recent ~120 places. Two views (v1.7): the 📋 List and the 🗺 Chart — a star map plotting every charted place across the universe. Brighter clusters hold more of your finds, favorites wear rings, home carries its ⌂, and a quiet crosshair marks where you are; tap any light to travel there . Your filters apply to both views. Planetfall auto-charts every world you stand on (the ⛳ Visited filter gathers them), and removing an entry offers its undo right in the list.

rows.title: Getting Around › The color language
rows.text: The expedition speaks in color, old-school MUD style — a tint means the same thing everywhere, and the words always carry the meaning too, so nothing is lost if you read past the color. Pop-ups and the 🔔 tray tint by event: red for harm and loss, gold for milestones and first contact, green for harvests, samples and mined hauls, calm blue for everything else. In the Chronicle , your champion reads cyan and the foe ember on every line; damage is yellow, criticals gold, misses dim, staggers flash, burns glow orange, mending green, lifesteal violet, thorns lime — a felled combatant falls in red, and the verdict wears its outcome: victory gold, defeat red. A world’s long-range glance tints each reading by family — water cyan, life green, signals violet. Elsewhere the language holds: the Compendium marks your Field Scout in cyan, the Star Atlas tints its badges, Cosmic Events wear their nature’s color, and a creature’s condition runs green → yellow → red as wounds deepen. A wave-off lands in harm red — a scrape, never a death. Field samples and touchdowns keep their gain green, and a landing that beats a hostile world arrives in milestone gold.

rows.title: Life & the Compendium › Discovering life
rows.text: From orbit a living world shows only its life signatures — the card blossoms when you land. Ground the world, then survey its biosphere : a deliberate act with teeth on hostile worlds — the danger percentage is your chance of being wounded by wildlife mid-survey, and wounds deepen with distance (a scrape in the home galaxy is survivable naked; the same claws in the Deep Field bite double and worse — scouts, the Reinforced Hull and crafted suits are how the far rings are survived). The survey always completes — you earned it. The survey reveals the roster; it catalogues nothing. Press 🐾 Tame for beasts and 🌿 Scavenge for flora, fungi and microbes — each attempt names its odds, rarer species resist harder, and crafted gear tips the hand. Every catch earns its Compendium page; there is no limit on trying. Or send a beast ahead: press Scout on any of your fauna’s cards to name it your Field Scout — it takes the hit in your place, wounds and all, mended the usual way with ♥ loved flora. A scout with nothing left is lost forever. A fresh scan can spark a spontaneous auto-hybrid with your existing collection. Conquered worlds scan safely — see Conquest . A thin slice of hostile worlds — molten, frozen, crushing — carries actual creatures, not just microbes. The odds run from about 1-in-70 on the friendliest extremes to 1-in-10,000 on the magma seas: the hardest landings hide the strangest finds.

rows.title: Life & the Compendium › The four kingdoms
rows.text: All life belongs to one of four kingdoms — 🦠 Microbe, 🌿 Flora, 🍄 Fungi, 🐾 Fauna — and is shelved in the Compendium by realm (Land Fauna, Aquatic Fauna, Colonial Life…). Kingdom decides what a creature can do: Fauna fight duels, defend worlds, and can be fed. Flora are medicine and meals — eaten by you or fed to beasts. All kingdoms can breed within their own kind. The sea grows kelp towers, reef-builders and sargassum rafts now; aerial-life worlds fly drifting veils. Extremophiles come with their own ways of living — vent-clingers, magma-swimmers, storm-riders — and worlds whose roster runs titanic sometimes show it breaking the horizon.

rows.title: Life & the Compendium › Rarity & grades
rows.text: Every species wears one of ten grades on a single ladder shared by creatures, plants, worlds and stars alike: Common → Uncommon → Notable → Rare → Exotic → Legendary → Mythic → Celestial → Primordial → Transcendent . Most expeditions live in the lower bands; the top grades grow vanishingly rare, and a Transcendent is a one-in-a-million roll — the province of master bloodlines and Apex Guardians . Rarity tints the card, pitches the discovery chime, and matters mechanically: Rarer flora heal more — and poison more. Rarer pairs are harder to breed but forge stronger bloodlines. Finding a Legendary-or-better species pays a ☄ Stardust bonus (first discovery only). Stars and worlds carry rarity too — but a world hides its grade until you land and stand on it; a star reveals its grade on survey . Rarer worlds yield richer conquest spoils. Chasing the rare grades? Size, glow, wild apex blood and deep hybrid generations all push a creature’s grade upward — a master bloodline can climb far past what nature rolls.

rows.title: Life & the Compendium › Reading a specimen card
rows.text: Tap any species in the Compendium to open its card: Five stat bars + Power — its battle strength, rolled deterministically from its genome (see The five stats ). ❤ HP & Condition — its battle pool, and whether it’s Healthy, Bruised, Injured or Critical. Wounds persist and dull every stat — see Injuries & recovery . ✧ Ability — its biome-themed combat trick (see Abilities ). ♥ Favors / ⊘ Dislikes — its feeding tastes (fauna only). ♞ Bloodline — brood (generations bred) and fed (meals taken) both permanently raise its stats. Buttons: ⇪ Code (share), ⚔ Duel , 🧬 Breed , 🌿 Feed , ✎ Rename .

rows.title: Life & the Compendium › Passive evolution
rows.text: Your Compendium is alive. As the cosmic clock ticks (one epoch ≈ every 4 minutes of play), two of your species quietly drift into a new hybrid on their own — the collection keeps surprising you the more you explore. Drift pauses at 500 species so your save stays healthy.

rows.title: Life & the Compendium › Sapience & civilizations
rows.text: Fauna roll an intelligence tier: Instinctive → Social → Tool-curious → Semi-sapient → Sapient . Whole worlds can host civilizations from stone-age to starfaring. A conquered world with a sapient native earns the Mind Signature — see The nine Signatures .

rows.title: Breeding & Feeding › Breeding
rows.text: Pick a specimen, press Breed , choose a same-kingdom mate. Both parents are consumed by the union — win or lose. The odds shown depend on the pair’s rarity — rare pairs are long shots. ☄ Stardust you’ve earned passively boosts odds (up to +15%) — see Stardust . Success forges a new bloodline : a hybrid child with boosted stats (+1 brood). Chain generations for monsters. The union’s experience goes to the child (+2, and +5 the first time you cross two particular species) — the parents are gone, so the newborn inherits the credit for them. A child inherits its parents’ brood but not their fed bloodline — a well-fed pair does not pass that strength on, and the preview says so before you commit. Failure loses both parents. Breed your spares, not your champions. Two extremophile parents breed a true extremophile; a mixed pair breeds back toward ordinary stock. A creature’s two-tone hide follows its accent gene, so children visibly carry their parents’ colors.

rows.title: Breeding & Feeding › Feeding beasts
rows.text: Fauna can be fed flora from your Compendium ( Feed on their card). The plant is always consumed. Every beast has tastes — two stat-flavors it loves, one it dislikes (shown on its card): A loved meal grows its fed bloodline — permanent strength, up to a ceiling. The first welcome meal and each new flavour discovered also teach the beast directly. Feeding is also medicine: a welcome meal mends a wounded beast, and loved flavors mend most. A disliked meal that goes badly can wound it further — see Injuries & recovery . Every meal carries a poison chance (worse for rare flora and disliked tastes) — a toxic roll poisons the beast, biting off a chunk of its condition; rarer flora bite far deeper. Only a beast whose strength is already spent dies of it — at zero, it’s gone. The Iron Gut ability shrugs toxins off.

rows.title: Breeding & Feeding › Injuries & recovery
rows.text: Wounds persist. A creature’s condition — Healthy → Bruised → Injured → Critical — lives on its specimen card, and the wounded fight below their strength (nearly half power at the brink). How they get hurt: winning a conquest by a thread leaves scars, and a disliked meal that goes badly can wound. Friendly duels are still pure sport — no harm done. How they heal: feed them. A welcome meal mends, the flavors a beast ♥ loves mend most, and rarer flora mend deeper. Wounds never fade on their own — medicine is a deliberate act. Injuries don’t travel in CFB codes — a shared creature arrives fresh. Newborn hybrids are born unhurt, whatever shape their parents were in.

rows.title: Breeding & Feeding › Eating flora (healing)
rows.text: Tap the ❤ heart by your HP bar to eat flora yourself. The plant is consumed and two things happen: You heal. Rarer flora restore more HP — but their poison chance is higher, and a toxic roll wounds you instead. The deadliest medicine heals hardest. You grow. Each plant nourishes one specific battle stat permanently (shown on its card). Vitality meals also raise your max HP. See The five stats .

rows.title: You, the Explorer › The five stats
rows.text: You fight with five stats, each starting at 50 and grown permanently by eating flora: Vitality — your life pool; sets max HP (×2) and duel toughness. Ferocity — attack power. Resilience — blunts incoming damage. Agility — initiative; who strikes first. Insight — critical-hit chance. Tap your nameplate to open your character sheet and inspect them. Creatures use the same five stats, rolled from their genomes.

rows.title: You, the Explorer › HP, hazards & death
rows.text: You can be wounded by scanning hostile worlds, by champion duty (losing a conquest you fought yourself), and by toxic flora. Your HP bar lives in the top bar; max HP = Vitality × 2. Heal by eating flora — tap the ❤ heart (see Eating flora ). Medicine never kills: a toxic meal can gut you to the brink — 1 HP — but eating flora is the one gamble that can’t end the expedition. (The same law as wave-offs: a scrape, never a grave.) At 0 HP the expedition ends — the universe is unchanged (it’s math), but your record starts over. Don’t scan furnace worlds at 12 HP.

rows.title: You, the Explorer › Ranks & expedition score
rows.text: Everything you do — surveying, cataloguing, breeding, settling, dueling — feeds your expedition score , and score climbs the ten ranks: Cadet → Scout → Pathfinder → Voyager → Pioneer → Star Cartographer → Mythic Wayfarer → Void Sovereign → Cosmic Luminary → Eternal Frontier . Your rank rides on your nameplate and on everything you share. Nameplate colors: every rank carries its own color, unlocked forever the moment you reach it. Pick any unlocked color from Settings → Nameplate — and Eternal Frontier unlocks the iridescent foil. Renaming yourself: open Settings → Nameplate and tap ✎ Change name anytime. Your record stays; only the name on it changes.

rows.title: You, the Explorer › Achievements
rows.text: Dozens of achievements track cataloguing, breeding, rarity hunting, conquest, stellar finds and exploration feats. They live on your character screen (tap your nameplate) under the Achievements fold — open it and each category shelf expands on its own. Many are secret handshakes with the universe: favorite a place, survive the brink, find a black hole…

rows.title: Combat › Duels & the Chronicle
rows.text: Duels are round-by-round creature battles. Agility decides who strikes first, Ferocity drives damage, Resilience blunts it, Insight lands criticals, Vitality sets the HP pool — and each side’s ✧ ability and 🛡 class arts bend the rules. Every fight is told as the Chronicle : named arts, first strikes, executes, thorn recoils, burn ticks, staggers, a death line — closing with a statistics ledger (hits, crits, biggest blow…). ⇪ Share the battle log at the end of any fight — a plain-text chronicle to paste anywhere, like a screenshot. Fights aren’t saved; legends are retold. Duel your own creatures from their cards, or paste a friend’s CFB- code. The same matchup always plays out identically, on every device. Friendly duels are sport: nothing is lost — but victories still feed your creature’s XP . Conquest is another story.

rows.title: Combat › Abilities & biome themes
rows.text: Every creature carries one ability from its habitat’s theme — fire, frost, storm, tide, stone, venom, void, sand, chem, psionic, wild (gliders lean storm, swimmers tide, burrowers stone…). Beside each theme’s named classics lives the ability matrix : sixteen archetype verbs — Smite, Aegis, Affliction, Fury, Ambush, Eye, Veil, Mending, Echo, Thirst, Thorns, Rend, Reckoning, Bulwark, Shock, Roulette — at five magnitudes (I–V) that climb with rarity: hundreds of abilities in all (“Fire Reckoning III”). Hybrids usually inherit their other parent’s archetype; sometimes they mutate something new. Apex Guardians fight with Sovereign arts at full magnitude. Every verb is balanced empirically — equal-stat win rates pinned near 50%, with honest counters. The ability is printed on the specimen card.

rows.title: Combat › Classes, XP & levels
rows.text: Every beast is born to a class — Warrior, Berserker, Necromancer, Assassin, Druid… over a hundred, with the legendary ones ( Titan, Worldbreaker, Avatar, Chosen One ) reserved for summit-grade creatures. A class grants innate arts : always-on powers that need no roll, printed on the specimen card. Power is built through wins and through care . Victories feed the XP bar — duels +8; conquests +20 and guardians +60, each climbing with the conquered world’s tier — and cataloguing a genuinely new species teaches your standing Field Scout +2. Keeping also counts: a welcome meal +1, a taste discovered +2, a bout survived +2, a fight taken to the wire +3, a conquest lost +3, and a defender pushed to the brink +5. Levels wake more innate arts (slots at level 3 and 6), never raw stats. A union pays its XP to the newborn — both parents are consumed, so the child is the only one left to carry it: +2 for the union, and +5 the first time you cross two particular species. Breeding fuses bloodlines: a hybrid usually inherits a class from its parents’ lineages — a Caster line crossed with a Martial line breeds toward Spellswords and Battlemages. Levels are your creature’s story — a shared code arrives at level 1.

rows.title: Combat › Conquering worlds
rows.text: Any world with fauna can be conquered. Press Conquer Planet on its survey card and choose one champion — yourself, or any fauna from your Compendium — to face the world’s apex native (its toughest beast; the picker shows your odds). The picker’s reading is simulated, not estimated : it runs the matchup 160 times and reports a band — Favored · Even · Dangerous · Overwhelming — with the sampled percentage and one line saying why. A sample that size cannot tell 0% from a half-percent, so it shows <1% and >99% rather than claiming a certainty it does not have. Win: the world flies your flag — bioscans are safe forever, ☄ Spoils of Conquest pay out, and the world can be harvested as you explore. Win ugly, pay for it: a champion that barely survives carries wounds home and fights below strength until mended — see Injuries & recovery . Lose with a wild-caught creature: it is gone forever. A hard-fought loss teaches your champion something — but a world only teaches it once . Lose with a bred champion: your bloodline crawls home Critical — broken, not dead. Mend it with flora it ♥ loves — a champion fielded while still Critical will not crawl home twice. Lose fighting yourself: you take the wound instead — it can beat you to the brink but never kill you, and below a quarter health you cannot lead a conquest at all (send a beast, or mend first). Worlds in farther frontier regions field tougher apex defenders. Conquest is also how most Signatures are claimed — see The nine Signatures .

rows.title: Combat › The Binder & the Fifty Paragons
rows.text: Open 🏆 Records and switch to the 🗂 Binder tab. You cannot collect individuals out of an infinite universe — so the Binder collects types: fixed pages of slots (every grade, every realm, every body plan, every ability theme…) that are the same for every explorer; your universe decides which specimen fills each. Sets are curated collections that pay a one-time ☄ Stardust bounty — claim them in the Binder when complete. The Fifty Paragons are named, one-of-a-kind deep-spectrum legends living on fixed worlds — the same fifty worlds for every explorer. Tap a silhouette to plot a course to its last-known world, then land and Discover Life to catalogue it. Share the coordinates — your friend hunts the very same legend.

rows.title: Combat › Apex Guardians
rows.text: About one fauna-bearing world in forty is ruled by a 👑 named Apex Guardian — a one-of-a-kind luminous titan wearing the ladder’s Transcendent summit, forced rather than rolled. The same guardian rules the same world for every explorer — share the coordinates and a friend faces the very same beast. A guarded world’s survey card names its ruler, grade and Power, and its conquest becomes a guardian challenge . Defeat it and the world is settled, the spoils pay a ruler’s ransom, and the guardian itself joins your Compendium — the fighter’s road to Transcendent. Lose and the usual price is paid: a champion creature is lost forever, or you take the wound. The breeder’s road also leads up: size, glow, wild blood and deep hybrid generations can push a bloodline to the summit without ever drawing a blade.

rows.title: Stardust & Progression › Stardust
rows.text: ☄ Stardust is the expedition’s soft currency. Lifetime Stardust earned passively raises your breeding odds (+1% per 50 earned, up to +15%). The faucets: ⛏ Harvests from settled worlds — see Harvesting . Spoils of Conquest — every world you settle pays out (rarer worlds pay more). Rare Find Bonus — first discovery of any Legendary+ species. First Arrival — reaching a system no expedition record precedes you in pays a small +2 ☄.

rows.title: Stardust & Progression › Harvesting
rows.text: Every settled world can be harvested for Stardust (rarer worlds yield more). A world replenishes as you explore — roughly 40 minutes of play, not 40 minutes of waiting — so an empire pays you for playing rather than for the calendar. The button lives on the world’s survey card; “Settled — replenishing” means keep exploring and come back. An empire of settled worlds is a steady Stardust income; visit your conquests.

rows.title: Stardust & Progression › Mining & the Cargo hold
rows.text: Dead worlds carry the elements. Every lifeless planet has a deterministic mineral profile by type — iron and titanium in rock, ices and helium-3 on frozen worlds, hydrogen in the gas giants, precious metals in metal worlds — and rarer worlds hide richer veins, up to exotics like Voidglass and Prismatium. Landing pays. Your first footfall on any world (home aside) collects field samples — a pinch of up to two of its elements and a few ☄ Stardust, richer on rarer worlds. Exploration stocks the hold all by itself. Prospecting takes boots on the ground: press a lifeless world’s Land button, or dive in and confirm the descent — planetfall is a ground survey , and the Mine Deposits button opens with it. (Gas giants, hothouses and molten worlds will fight the landing — see Landing .) (🛰 Deep Scanners read the veins from orbit, but the drills still need a surface under them.) The drills run in bursts. Press ⛏ Mine once and the rig pulls a burst — up to ten pulls over a quarter minute — then the drills stand down and want another press. Stop early anytime; a vein can still run dry mid-burst. Every haul varies, and sometimes a rich strike hits a rare pocket. Reserves are finite: the card counts the pulls left, and a world mined to nothing stays mined out forever (there are always more worlds). Crafted mining rigs multiply every haul, and the Auto-Extractor keeps pulling while you’re away — collect on your next visit. Everything lands in your 🧰 Cargo hold — it lives on your character screen now, beneath the paperdoll (tap your nameplate, or the 🧰 shortcut that appears with your first cargo). The hold is a Diablo bag under your portrait: a grid of slots — ingots for metals, shards for ices, flasks for gases, cut gems for the exotics. Spending them happens at the 🛠 Shipyard (the dock — or the right rail on desktop): the Fabricator and the Research Bench live with the ship they build — and a crafted pack in your Module socket grows the bags themselves. See Research & ships .

rows.title: Stardust & Progression › Stellar skimming & the veins
rows.text: Stars are mines too. Survey a star, then ☀ Skim Corona pulls stellar material straight from its fire — hot bright stars give Stellar Plasma , dead dense remnants give Coronium , cool dwarfs give nothing. Skimming rides the Jump Drive’s shielding, and each star’s reachable corona is finite. Mind the dead stars: a remnant’s corona bites the unshielded for 3 HP a pass — the Corona Scoop (Shipyard, costs one hand-skimmed Plasma) ends the bite, ladles +1 per pass, and reaches a deeper corona (an exhausted star reopens when you build it). Three special veins can ride a world’s survey card past its base minerals: the biome vein (a living world’s gated exotic), the cosmic vein (Primordial-and-up worlds only — foundational and reality-breaking materials), and the ✦ exceptional vein (~1 world in 7 hides an ultra-pure seam of one of its own minerals — found only once you land). Exceptional units stack as a ✦ sub-count on the same material card, count one grade higher, and the Fabricator spends them first — forge a piece entirely from exceptional stock and it arrives Exceptionally Forged , carrying a bonus affix like conquest spoils.

rows.title: Stardust & Progression › Research & ships
rows.text: The engineer’s track, parallel to the Prime Codex: the Prime Codex is your legend, the Research Bench is your capability. Research costs mined elements + ☄ Stardust: 🛰 Deep Scanners — survey cards reveal mineral veins from orbit. 🛡 Reinforced Hull — hostile bioscans wound you 25% lighter. 🧪 Xenobotany Lab — flora meals nourish one extra stat point. The drive ladder — 🚀 Fusion → ⚛ Antimatter → 🌀 Warp Fold. Hyperlane travel scales with real distance; each drive cuts it, and Warp Fold makes every jump arrive in a breath. Distance is never a wall — only a wait, and only ever a short one.

rows.title: Stardust & Progression › The Fabricator & gear
rows.text: The Fabricator lives at the 🛠 Shipyard (the dock — or the right rail on desktop) — your ship, her systems, and both workbenches in one place. It turns ore into capability, three rungs up: T1 basic parts (plates, wire, chips, weave) → T2 components (drive coils, nav cores, hull segments) → T3 ship systems and explorer gear . Recipes are fixed and identical for every explorer; nothing waits on a timer. Ship systems build once and stay built: the ⚡ Jump Drive, 📡 Long-Range Array and 🌌 Intergalactic Drive open the travel rings (see Chapters ); the 🤖 Auto-Extractor keeps mining every world you’ve worked while you’re away. Gear equips on YOU. Your character screen (tap your nameplate) shows your explorer head to boots, with nine sockets pinned to the body — Helmet at the head, Earpiece at the ear, Necklace below the chin, Suit on the chest, Gloves and Tool at the hands, Leggings, Boots, and the Module — the 🎒 pack on your shoulder. Mining rigs and gloves multiply hauls; suits, visors and leggings blunt field wounds (the T3 hazard suits open molten, crushing and frozen worlds to nearly-sure landings); boots, greaves and the module ladder steady landings up to the Gravitic Anchor, which never waves off; earpieces and necklaces sharpen first contact, rich strikes, meals and travel. Risk is the frontier — gear is how you tame it. Every roll in the game (landing, contact, bioscan) has a crafted answer. The hold is three tabs (character screen): Materials — every element stacks by substance, grouped by family, never slot pressure; Craftables — parts and components by kind; Gear — the slot grid the pack module grows. Tap any item for its card : rarity frame, level, its ✦ affix lines with ranges, and a compare against what you’re wearing. Equip and ♺ Salvage are buttons on the card — salvage breaks a piece back into some of its materials (a confirm guards it; toggle in Settings › Gameplay, and Salvage All Junk clears unequipped commons in one press). Affixes — seeded bonus stats on worn gear — come from conquest spoils, or from forging with pure ✦ exceptional stock.

rows.title: Stardust & Progression › Chapters
rows.text: ⬆ The Chapters are the mainline: three of them, pinned at the top of your Charters board, that carry a new explorer from one rock to the whole sky. The rings, in order: Sol. New expeditions start locked to the home system — the entire sky stays visible and surveyable (looking is always free; moving is what you earn). Mine Sol’s dead worlds and build the ⚡ Jump Drive . The Neighborhood. The nearby stars open. Hunt life, settle a world, and build the 📡 Long-Range Array for the whole galaxy. Beyond the Rim. Master the trades and build the 🌌 Intergalactic Drive — from there the Prime Codex Signatures extend your reach, ring by ring, exactly as they always have. The spectrum expands with the rings. Rarity is a ladder of distance: the Neighborhood catalogues up to Legendary , the home galaxy up to Primordial , and each region beyond makes Transcendent finds steadily less rare — until the Deep Field, where the ladder’s summit lives. The strangest finds live farthest out; guardians, Paragons and your own bred bloodlines are beyond the law.

rows.title: The Prime Codex › The Elemental Signatures (nine titans)
rows.text: The nine elements are the universe’s master test. Each elemental force is embodied by a unique named titan — the same for every explorer. You won’t know a titan waits until you land and survey , and it may or may not be present when you arrive. Face it, send your strongest bred and tamed champions, prevail, and you master that element. The nine, staggered from near to far: Earth · Fire · Air · Wind · Water — the basics, near home and its neighboring rings. Electric · Poison — the middle reach, the Local Cluster and Near Field. Void · Prism — far out, past the Deep Field. Every element you master recovers a relic blueprint — nine unique, signature-tier pieces of gear (one per socket) that only the Fabricator of a master can forge. The Codex panel (✦, left rail) names each element’s titan and how far out it dwells, and tracks the blueprints you hold. This is where the whole game becomes one: land, mine and tame and heal, craft and breed stronger champions — then master the titans one element at a time, until you are master of them all.

rows.title: The Prime Codex › Frontier regions
rows.text: You begin charted for the Solar Reach . Each Signature claimed pushes your charter outward — the Local Cluster, the Near Field, the Deep Field, the Outer Dark , and finally the Frontier . Travel beyond your charter is blocked until you’ve earned it, and farther regions field tougher apex defenders with stranger life.

rows.title: The Prime Codex › Endings & the Celestial Frontier
rows.text: Master all nine elements and the Celestial Frontier reveals itself — and asks what kind of Pathfinder you are. Your choice becomes your legacy (some legacies must be earned through deeds beyond the Prime Codex). The universe stays open afterward: you cannot finish the infinite, only master it.

rows.title: The Living Universe › Cosmic events
rows.text: The universe is alive on every timescale: somewhere a star is always dying, and rarer spectacles cycle by the minute, hour, day, week, month, year and decade. Open Cosmic Events (left rail) to see what’s live and travel to it. Because everything is deterministic, every explorer sees the same event at the same moment — witnessing one is a shared experience. The 📜 Witness Log at the top of the panel remembers every sky you saw with your own eyes.

rows.title: The Living Universe › One universe, no server
rows.text: There is no server and no download — the entire universe is generated from seeds, on your device, on demand. The same coordinates always hold the same galaxy, the same world, the same creature, for everyone, forever. That’s what makes share codes work, duels fair, and events shared. The universe needs no saving; only your story is saved.

rows.title: Settings & Saving › Settings
rows.text: The dock holds your five boards — it rides the BOTTOM edge on phones and the RIGHT rail on desktop, with ⚙ Settings and the ? Guide beside it either way. The ⚙ panel (dock ⚙) has four tabs. Display : Text size (A/A+/A++), Text tone (Soft / Bright / Max — brighter tones lift body text toward white and shift bold to gold), Font (Grotesk / System / Mono), Explorer name , and Tooltips (the short hints on hover, keyboard focus, or long-press — turn them off once you’re fluent). Graphics : Visual effects (particle bursts), Screen shake , Motion (Auto follows your device’s reduce-motion preference; Reduced stills the travel tunnel, shake, confetti and shimmer), and Panel tint (a glass slider — drag from airy liquid glass to a near-solid backing; a floor keeps text readable). Gameplay : Confirm before salvaging — the guard that asks before an item (or Salvage All) breaks gear down for parts. Audio : Sound (the master — off silences everything at once, including a world’s ambience), the Volume slider, Creature voices (every beast has its own call, inherited and blended when you breed), Battle sound (blow-by-blow impact in duels and conquests), and Notifications (silences pop-ups; the 🔔 tray still logs everything). All persist with your save.

rows.title: Settings & Saving › Your save & reset
rows.text: Your expedition saves automatically to this browser on this device — no account, no cloud. Clearing site data clears the expedition, so export your best creatures as CFB codes if you’re attached. ↺ Reset Game in Settings erases everything after a confirm — the universe itself is unharmed; it’s math.

rows.title: v1.8.9 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🐘 A CREATURE IS ONE SIZE EVERYWHERE — a beast from a long bloodline could be described as “tiny” on its card while the game quietly classified it as Megafauna, handing it a rarity boost and noticeably more vitality than its size should allow. Size now means the same thing on the card, in the fight, in its habitat classification and in the Compendium’s Size Classes.

rows.title: v1.8.9 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🏝 SIZE CLASSES AND HABITAT READINGS AGREE WITH THE CARD — the same mismatch could file a bred creature under the wrong realm, or count it toward a world’s megafauna when it was nothing of the kind.

rows.title: v1.8.9 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: 📐 ONE DEFINITION OF SIZE — the six places that read the size gene now share a single helper rather than each deciding for themselves. The check that guards it proves a bred creature and its equivalent smaller size are treated identically, and it fails against the previous build.

rows.title: v1.8.8 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🌍 SETTLED WORLDS NOW PAY YOU FOR EXPLORING, NOT FOR WAITING — a conquered world used to replenish on the calendar: one harvest per hour, whether you were playing or the game was closed. It now replenishes as you explore, roughly forty minutes of play per world. If you play, you earn faster than before. If you leave the game closed for a week, your empire waits for you rather than paying out for time you did not spend. This is the same clock your biosphere pools and creature evolution have always used.

rows.title: v1.8.8 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: ☄ AN EMPIRE YOU LEFT BEHIND PAYS ONCE ON YOUR RETURN — every settled world is ready the first time you open this version, so a long-standing empire is not penalised for the change.

rows.title: v1.8.8 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⏱ THE HARVEST TIMER NO LONGER TRUSTS YOUR DEVICE CLOCK — changing your device’s date could persuade a settled world it had been replenishing for hours. Harvest no longer reads the device clock at all, so there is nothing left to persuade.

rows.title: v1.8.8 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🔘 THE HARVEST BUTTON AND THE HARVEST AGREE — the button face, the survey card and the action itself now read readiness from one place, so a world can never look ready and then refuse.

rows.title: v1.8.8 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: 🧪 A NEW CHECK PROVES THE CLOCK CANNOT BE WOUND — it moves a simulated device clock forward a full day and asserts that a settled world stays exactly as ready as the play-time it has earned. It fails against the previous build, which is the only reason to trust it.

rows.title: v1.8.7 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🧬 YOUR BRED CREATURES KEEP THEIR SIZE — a creature from a long bloodline could come back from a reload as a different size entirely, usually the largest one, with the vitality and portrait to match. Its voice, its body and its Size Classes slot all moved with it. Bloodlines now read the same before and after a reload, and a creature you exported yesterday still matches the one in your Compendium today.

rows.title: v1.8.7 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📱 THE DOCK STAYS REACHABLE DURING TRAINING — on smaller phones, opening the Compendium, Star Atlas or Charters board during Field Training could cover the entire bottom dock, leaving no way to reach the Compendium, Atlas, Shipyard, Charters, Settings or Guide until the board was closed.

rows.title: v1.8.7 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 💡 THE "YOU SEEM STUCK" POINTER NO LONGER DISAPPEARS — acting on the suggestion chip could make it vanish for a player with no objective, which is exactly the player who needed it. If you have nothing on your slate, the chip now always offers a next step.

rows.title: v1.8.7 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🗓 WEEKLY CHARTERS — the limit added last release is honest about what it does now; the note in the code no longer claims more than the code delivers.

rows.title: v1.8.7 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: ⚔ FASTER CONQUEST PICKER — the odds meter rebuilt the defending creature’s stats once per row. It now computes them once for the whole list.

rows.title: v1.8.7 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: 🧪 TWO MORE OUTCOME TESTS — one proves a long bloodline survives a save-and-reload with its size intact, the other proves the training dock stays pressable behind every raised board on every phone size. Both were checked against the previous build first, to confirm they actually catch the bug they were written for.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🎓 THE LESSON CARD STAYS READABLE — opening the Compendium, Star Atlas, Charters or Records during Field Training could draw the board straight over the lesson you were following, hiding both the instruction and the Skip button. On a tablet at the "open a shelf, then tap a specimen" step the card was completely buried. Boards now always make room for the lesson.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⚔ DUEL VICTORIES FINALLY PAY — winning a friendly duel awarded your creature nothing at all. Neither did surviving a bout or taking one to the wire. All three now land the XP the Guide has always advertised, and a win no longer quietly eats the cooldown that the next one needed.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🎯 THE CONQUEST ODDS TELL THE TRUTH — the matchup meter cached its estimate too aggressively, so feeding or breeding a champion (or a defender picking up a world bonus) could leave it showing the old number — occasionally the exact opposite of the real result.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🧬 A FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND LINEAGE IS ACTUALLY A FIRST — the lineage bonus announced itself on every successful pairing instead of the first of each kind.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📋 THE QUEST LOG KEEPS ITS HANDLE — while the objective chip was showing a "you seem stuck" suggestion, tapping it could no longer open the quest log — exactly when you would want to check what you were meant to be doing.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📏 SIZE READS THE SAME ON THE CARD AND IN THE FIGHT — a heavily bred creature could describe itself as one size on its specimen sheet while fighting at another.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ❤ BLOODLINE NUMBERS STOP OVERSHOOTING — a very well-fed beast, or a child of two large broods, could display a fed/brood count above the game’s own 200 ceiling and then snap back after a reload.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🎨 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🐣 THE SPECIMEN SHEET EXPLAINS CARE — the XP line still said victories were the only thing that fed a creature, which has not been true since The Connection. It now names first tastes, unions and new lineages alongside duels, conquests and guardians.

rows.title: v1.8.6 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🗓 WEEKLY CHARTERS KEEP THEIR CADENCE — the weekly slate could be persuaded to reroll far more often than weekly, making completed contracts claimable again.

rows.title: v1.8.6 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🔊 CREATURE VOICES USE THEIR FULL RANGE — five of the traits that colour a voice were being folded into far fewer variations than they have, so different creatures sounded more alike than they should. Diets in particular now sound distinct.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: 🧪 REWARDS ARE NOW TESTED BY OUTCOME — a new check plays a real duel and then reads the ledger to confirm the XP arrived. The previous test called the award function directly, which is why a reward that the game never actually granted could pass it in every build.

rows.title: v1.8.6 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: 📐 THE LAYOUT GATE MEASURES THE LESSON CARD — the browser-based gate grew 80 checks that sample the training card across ten viewports with each board raised, in both card positions.

rows.title: v1.8.5 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🚀 THE FIRST SCREEN ANSWERS AT ONCE — on a phone, a brand-new expedition spent several seconds building world art you could not see yet, behind the naming screen, so the very first thing you touched did not respond. The art now waits its turn.

rows.title: v1.8.5 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: ⏱ A COLD-BOOT GATE — the moment the first screen becomes answerable is now measured in a real browser on a throttled phone, because a screen that is drawn is not the same as a screen that answers. That difference was five seconds, and nothing here was watching for it.

rows.title: v1.8.5 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: 🤖 THE PLAYTEST FLEET PRESSES REAL BUTTONS — a new harness tier takes its actions through the same controls you use instead of reaching past them, so a button that is present but wired to nothing fails here first.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🗺 THE LESSON’S OWN SCREEN COMES FORWARD — on phones, Earth’s survey card sat on top of every board, so the two lessons that ask you to open the Star Atlas and the Compendium opened them underneath it. The Compendium button could not be pressed at all. Whatever the current lesson points at now takes the front — except on the landing step, where the card is the thing you need.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📱 THE DOCK IS NEVER BURIED — the survey card stops above the bottom dock instead of running over the buttons a lesson is pointing at.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🪐 THE PLANETSIDE READS CLEARLY DURING TRAINING — the landing view was sliding under the guidance card, hiding its own heading. It settles below the lesson now, so you can read both.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⚙ SETTINGS OPENS OVER A LESSON — the guidance card was covering the Settings panel, the Audio tab especially, on almost every screen size.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🧬 A UNION’S EXPERIENCE REACHES THE CHILD — both parents are consumed by breeding, and the experience was paid to one of them, so it vanished as it was earned. The newborn carries it now: +2 for the union, +5 the first time you cross two particular species.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🛡 A BOUT SURVIVED FINALLY COUNTS — two of the eight ways a creature earns experience (surviving a bout, and a fight taken to the wire) could never actually pay out. They do now.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 💡 THE NUDGE REACHES THE PLAYERS WHO NEED IT — the suggestion that appears when nothing has moved for a while could only ever show for someone who already had a goal. The player with nothing on — the one most likely to give up — was the only one who could never be offered a next step.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ☄ SKIMMING A CORONA IS PROGRESS — the game was treating an active skim as if you had stopped playing, and suggested you go do something else.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📋 THE QUEST LOG IS LIVE — it was a snapshot taken when you opened it: charter progress never moved while you watched. It now updates with the objective, closes on Escape, and never strands on screen without a handle.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🔇 SOUND OFF MEANS OFF — switching Sound off left a world’s ambience playing underneath.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⚔ THE MATCHUP METER STOPS ROUNDING TO CERTAINTY — hopeless and near-certain matchups read <1% and >99% instead of a flat 0% or 100%, and the picker builds its estimate far more cheaply.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ❤ THE HEAL TARGET IS A FIXED SIZE — it was sized from the heart glyph, whose width varies by device, and computed under the 44px minimum on phones.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ♿ GUIDANCE BUTTONS NO LONGER CLAIM TO BE DISABLED, AND NO LONGER GO DEAD — the shortfall buttons on a specimen card and in the Fabricator now answer when pressed, name what is missing, and sound like a refusal. A verb a lesson has blocked answers too, instead of doing nothing at all.

rows.title: v1.8.4 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🔒 A SPECIES MUST BE CAUGHT TO BE CATALOGUED — tapping a life-form in a world’s roster added it to your Compendium outright, skipping the tame or scavenge attempt entirely. It now points you at the verb that earns it.

rows.title: v1.8.4 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🍽 A WELCOME MEAL IS THE FIRST ONE — the welcome-meal bonus paid on every loved meal forever, and a creature’s fed bloodline had no ceiling, so a card could promise strength the fighter did not have.

rows.title: v1.8.4 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: ⚔ A LESSON IS LEARNED FROM A WORLD ONCE — losing a conquest was never recorded, so the same world paid its consolation experience on every attempt, indefinitely.

rows.title: v1.8.4 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 📜 WEEKLY CHARTERS NO LONGER PAY FOR OLD GROUND — a weekly landfall charter completed the moment you accepted it, from worlds you had visited long before, and re-rolled on every clock change.

rows.title: v1.8.4 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🌍 HARVESTS KEEP THEIR OWN CLOCK — a settled world’s hourly harvest measured only the device clock.

rows.title: v1.8.4 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 💾 A SAVED CREATURE CANNOT CARRY BATTLEFIELD MODIFIERS HOME — the same fields a shared code has always stripped are now stripped on load.

rows.title: v1.8.4 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🧪 THE BREEDING PREVIEW TELLS THE TRUTH — the child’s power range was built from the parents’ fed bloodlines, which a child does not inherit. The range now reflects what the child will actually be, and the card says so.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🔊 Audio
rows.text: 🐾 CREATURES SOUND FAR MORE LIKE THEMSELVES — the voice read only three things about a creature, so the whole vocabulary was 540 calls: in a collection of fifty, nine in ten had a twin. It now reads its trait, build, gait, diet and senses too.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🔊 Audio
rows.text: 🎭 TEMPERAMENT IS THE GENE THE CARD PRINTS — the voice’s character was keyed to the wrong gene entirely, so the most aggressive creatures in the game carried some of the meekest voices.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🔊 Audio
rows.text: 🦇 NO CREATURE IS PINNED AT THE CEILING — about one in fifty voiced at the top of the range, all of them bats, where size and temperament stopped mattering and the call was simply shrill.

rows.title: v1.8.4 🔊 Audio
rows.text: ✅ A SUCCESSFUL ACTION SOUNDS LIKE ONE — the confirming tone existed but was never once played, so the contrast the refusal tone depends on only had one side.

rows.title: v1.8.4 📖 Guide
rows.text: 📖 THE GUIDE CATCHES UP — the class topic covers experience earned through care and says where a union’s experience lands; breeding repeats it where a breeder will look; conquest explains that the meter is simulated rather than estimated; and Settings lists the Creature voices and Battle sound switches.

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🗺 THE LESSON’S OWN SCREEN COMES FORWARD — on phones, Earth’s survey card sat on top of every board, so the two lessons that ask you to open the Star Atlas and the Compendium opened them underneath it, with no way through. Whatever the current lesson points at now takes the front, and the card steps back — except on the landing step, where the card is the thing you need.

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📱 THE DOCK IS NEVER BURIED — the survey card now stops above the bottom dock instead of running over the chips a lesson is pointing at.

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🪐 THE PLANETSIDE READS CLEARLY DURING TRAINING — the landing view was sliding under the guidance card, hiding its own heading. It now settles below the lesson, the way every other dialog does, so you can read both.

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⚙ SETTINGS OPENS OVER A LESSON — the guidance card was covering the Settings panel (the Audio tab especially) on almost every screen size. Settings you opened yourself now comes to the front.

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🧬 A UNION’S EXPERIENCE REACHES THE CHILD — both parents are consumed by breeding, and the experience was being paid to one of them, so it vanished the moment it was earned. The newborn now carries it: +2 for the union, +5 the first time you cross two particular species. (That bonus also only ever recognised “fauna with fauna” before, so it never meant what it said.)

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🔇 SOUND OFF MEANS OFF — switching Sound off left a world’s ambience still playing underneath. It stops immediately now.

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⚔ THE MATCHUP METER STOPS ROUNDING TO CERTAINTY — 160 simulated duels cannot tell 0% from a half-percent, so hopeless and near-certain matchups now read <1% and >99% instead of a flat 0% or 100%.

rows.title: v1.8.3 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ♿ GUIDANCE BUTTONS NO LONGER CLAIM TO BE DISABLED — the Breed and Feed buttons that explain what you are missing are pressable and always were, but they told screen readers the opposite. They now announce what they actually do.

rows.title: v1.8.3 📖 Guide
rows.text: 📖 THE GUIDE CATCHES UP — the class topic now covers experience earned through care , not victories alone, and says where a union’s experience lands; breeding repeats it where a breeder will look; conquest explains that the meter is simulated rather than estimated; and Settings lists the Creature voices and Battle sound switches.

rows.title: v1.8.2 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🍽 THE MEAL AND THE UNION KEEP THEIR CARD — the feed and breed lessons were closing the specimen card and then asking you to open one again. The card stays open now (its own Feed and Breed buttons are the target), and if you close it, reopening any beast works just as well.

rows.title: v1.8.2 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ❤ A CALMER HEART — the ❤ keeps its full-size touch target, but its glow and focus ring now hug the heart itself instead of drawing a large box across the HP bar.

rows.title: v1.8.2 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📊 THE HP BAR STAYS IN ITS TRACK — the fill can no longer paint past its own edge.

rows.title: v1.8.1 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 📋 A REAL QUEST LOG — the objective pill was one line with a bare “+1”. Tap it now and it unfolds into a compact log: your chapter goal and every accepted charter, each with live progress, and a way straight to the board. Tap again to fold it away.

rows.title: v1.8.1 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🪐 THE PLANETSIDE IS NEVER COVERED — during training the survey card could sit on top of the landing view, hiding the very payoff the lesson is about. The card now yields the screen whenever the Planetside is open.

rows.title: v1.8.1 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🗂 NOTHING OPENS ITSELF — the Compendium’s shelves and the Fabricator’s categories now start closed everywhere, training included; the two lessons that relied on a pre-opened drawer simply ask you to open one, which is a better lesson anyway.

rows.title: v1.8.0 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 🗣 EVERY CREATURE HAS A VOICE — and it is truly its own. Earth’s animals sound like what they are: wolves roar, sparrows chirp, whales sing, rattlesnakes hiss, cicadas drone. Alien life speaks from its own genome. And when you breed , the child inherits BOTH parents’ voices — a roarer crossed with a chirper carries each of them, and its descendants drift further into the unknown with every generation. No two bloodlines sound alike, and the same creature sounds identical for every explorer who holds its code.

rows.title: v1.8.0 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: ⚔ THE FIGHT HAS A SOUND — duels and conquests were nearly silent. Every blow now lands with weight, critical hits ring above the impact, and ability strikes carry their own voice.

rows.title: v1.8.0 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 🪐 PLANETFALL ARRIVES — dropping onto a world opens with a chord, and the world itself murmurs underneath while you look out over it: wind on the tundra, surf on the ocean shelves, a low furnace on the magma seas.

rows.title: v1.8.0 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 💡 THE GAME TELLS YOU WHAT TO DO NEXT — when nothing has moved for a while, the objective chip stops repeating your goal and offers a concrete next step you can actually take right now, and takes you there.

rows.title: v1.8.0 🧭 Gameplay
rows.text: 🚫 NO MORE DEAD TAPS — every “can’t” now names what is missing, why, and where to get it, with a button that takes you there. Breed and Feed wear their shortfall on the button before you press them, and a blocked action sounds different from a successful one.

rows.title: v1.8.0 🧭 Gameplay
rows.text: ⚖ HONEST CONQUEST ODDS — the win estimate was a rough power comparison that could read 50% when the truth was zero, printed beside a warning that losing costs your champion forever. It now runs the real fight hundreds of times behind the scenes and reports what actually happens: Favored, Even, Dangerous or Overwhelming, with the reason why.

rows.title: v1.8.0 🧭 Gameplay
rows.text: 🧬 CARE COUNTS — creatures now gain experience from a welcome meal, a taste discovered, a successful union, a first-of-its-kind lineage, a bout survived, a fight taken to the wire and a conquest lost, not from victories alone.

rows.title: v1.8.0 🧭 Gameplay
rows.text: 🔮 BREEDING SHOWS ITS PROMISE — a mate’s row now previews the power band and the rarity a child could reach. Never the exact result: the reveal is the point.

rows.title: v1.8.0 🧭 Gameplay
rows.text: ✦ WORLDS NAME THEIR MOST NOTABLE RESIDENT, and every creature card speaks its temperament.

rows.title: v1.8.0 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🔊 TWO NEW SWITCHES — Settings › Audio can silence creature voices and battle sound independently. Both start on.

rows.title: v1.7.21 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🌍 EARTH REALLY KEEPS ITS HISTORY — the last fix only held if you skipped training early. Training step 4 asks you to re-chart Earth, so on any completed run your original entry was quietly replaced by a fresh one. Your ☆ favourite, discovery date, badge and notes now merge back onto it every time, and they ride the save so a mid-training reload keeps them too.

rows.title: v1.7.21 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🧬 TRAINING NO LONGER LEAVES A MARK — an emergency restore could bake the practice lessons permanently into your record (hybrid counts, feeding and breeding tallies, even the heal step’s stat growth). It now restores the numbers you had before you started.

rows.title: v1.7.21 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ❤ A REAL HEART, FOR FREE — the 44px heal target is back to costing zero layout: v1.7.20 bought it with ~26px of permanent header height on every device.

rows.title: v1.7.21 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🛟 AN HONEST FAILURE MESSAGE — if a restore ever cannot complete, the game no longer points you toward the button that erases everything.

rows.title: v1.7.21 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⏰ CLOCK SANITY, FINAL FORM — weekly charters are no longer “repaired” at startup, which is exactly when a device clock is least trustworthy; a lagging clock can no longer wipe a week you were part-way through.

rows.title: v1.7.21 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🎓 THE LESSON CARD KEEPS ITS PLACE — the spotlight ring no longer outranks the card that explains it, and the ? popover is reachable during training again.

rows.title: v1.7.20 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🛟 THE RELOAD PATH, PROVEN — the mid-training reload restore is finally whole: the genome sanitizer it needed is now shared across the codebase, the snapshot survives a failure anywhere in its own construction, and recovery restores your Compendium before it says a word. If it ever cannot, it now tells you the truth instead of a comforting lie.

rows.title: v1.7.20 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🌍 EARTH KEEPS ITS HISTORY — restarting training restores your Atlas entry for Earth exactly as it was, ☆ favourite and all, instead of rebuilding it as a fresh stub.

rows.title: v1.7.20 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⏰ CLOCKS CAN’T TOUCH YOUR CHARTERS — a lagging device clock no longer rewinds your weekly slate (which both wiped honest progress and let the week be re-rolled).

rows.title: v1.7.20 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⌨ FOCUS AND KEYS — closing a dialog over an open survey card now returns your focus properly, the star map accepts its advertised arrow/Enter/zoom keys under a screen reader again, and the name field holds the 16px floor that stops iPad Safari zooming.

rows.title: v1.7.20 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ❤ A REAL HEAL TARGET — the heart now measures a true 44×44 on every device, and the training spotlight no longer draws over the lesson card that explains it.

rows.title: v1.7.19 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🛟 THE RELOAD PATH, TRULY SAFE — round four of testing caught three of our fixes placed where they couldn’t run. The worst let a mid-training reload wipe the Compendium; the restart snapshot now restores through any reload, proven by a new automated journey that walks that exact path on every release.

rows.title: v1.7.19 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⚔ THE TIE COIN ACTUALLY FLIPS — the mirror-match fairness fix read a field that didn’t exist; exact ties now genuinely break on the seeded coin.

rows.title: v1.7.19 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 📱 THE TABLET TARGETS ACTUALLY GROW — the 44px rules had landed in the wrong stylesheet and lost the cascade; they now apply, along with the titan-title clamp and landscape caps that shared the defect.

rows.title: v1.7.19 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🎓 RESTART POLISH — restarting training no longer double-counts your hybrids, falsely pops achievements, rebuilds Earth’s Atlas entry as a stub (your ☆ and history survive), or hides the lesson spotlight behind the survey card.

rows.title: v1.7.19 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🧮 SMALL TRUTHS — the 900th First Arrival pays again, a forward clock jump can’t freeze the weekly charters, the last two low-contrast texts stepped up, Text Size reaches the settings rows, and the star map introduces itself without hijacking screen-reader browse mode.

rows.title: v1.7.18 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🛟 RESTART TRAINING KEEPS ITS PROMISE — restarting the Field Training now truly leaves your expedition untouched: your Compendium, cargo, exceptional stock, items and every equipped piece come back exactly as they were, even if you reload mid-training. And a restarted training no longer dead-ends at the Atlas lesson.

rows.title: v1.7.18 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⚖ THE ARENA TELLS THE TRUTH — burning abilities no longer tick twice per round (Cinderburn was winning 98% of fights through armor), exact-HP ties no longer secretly favor you, defensive builds can actually win (the damage floor now respects mitigation instead of erasing it), and the battle log names the real first mover. All 17 fighting styles and all 55 rolled abilities are measured inside fair bands now.

rows.title: v1.7.18 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🥋 26 CLASSES WAKE UP — Brawler, Ronin, Psion, Chaos Mage, Eldritch Horror and 21 others were silently missing their innate arts due to two misspelled ability names; every class now grants what its description promises.

rows.title: v1.7.18 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⏰ THE CLOCK CAN’T PAY YOU — backward clock changes no longer refund mining reserves, re-roll the weekly charter slate, or (past 900 systems) turn First Arrival into an endless stardust faucet.

rows.title: v1.7.18 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 👑 COSMIC GEAR RULES ITS TIER — the Protomatter Carapace, Coronal Aegis and Dark Matter Bore were weaker than ordinary tier-2 gear; all three now stand above the ladder they crown.

rows.title: v1.7.18 ♿ Accessibility & Touch
rows.text: 📱 THE TABLET BAND GETS REAL TARGETS — Surface Pro and iPad Pro sizes now receive full 44px touch targets, the 16px input floor and safe-area clearance; the ❤ heal control grew from 12px to a real fingertip target.

rows.title: v1.7.18 ♿ Accessibility & Touch
rows.text: ⌨ FOCUS COMES HOME — closing any dialog with Escape returns your keyboard focus where it was; achievement and stat folds are keyboard-reachable; the star map introduces itself to assistive technology instead of hiding from it.

rows.title: v1.7.18 ♿ Accessibility & Touch
rows.text: 🔎 SMALL FIXES WITH BIG READS — dimmed text everywhere steps up to readable contrast, the training card scrolls instead of pushing its button off-screen and honors your Text Size, titan titles stop truncating, Atlas rows wrap instead of crushing names, and toasts stop blocking the survey card.

rows.title: v1.7.17 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🎓 LESSONS SHOW THEIR WORK — during training the survey card and lesson surfaces now sit above the boards and dock instead of behind them (Earth’s card was buried on the landing step), and the training dialogue only takes the very top on the one step whose full-screen sheet demanded it.

rows.title: v1.7.17 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🔎 A SLIMMER SEARCH — the phone search pill trades some width and padding for a tidier top bar; the 16px type that keeps iOS from zooming stays.

rows.title: v1.7.16 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🗂 TRAINING TIDIES UP AFTER ITSELF — the lessons open the shelf they teach (Compendium, Fabricator), but those shelves stayed expanded after graduation; a fresh veteran now opens both to the tidy closed index.

rows.title: v1.7.16 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🎓 THE NAMEPLATE LESSON STAYS ON TOP — the character sheet was covering the training card (and its Got It button) on phones, making the step look like it vanished; during training the card now outranks every board.

rows.title: v1.7.16 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⛳ EVERY OBJECTIVE WEARS ITS COUNT — one-shot charters on the dock chip showed no progress digits and read like the old dead pill; the tracker now always shows 0 / 1 → 1 / 1.

rows.title: v1.7.15 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 📖 THE GUIDE CATCHES UP WITH v1.7 — the Star Atlas topic teaches the 🗺 Chart view, auto-charting and the in-list undo; the survey topic covers worlds of renown, on-the-ground vein grades and ⬆ Leave this world; the Charters topic explains the live objective chip and the always-yours mainline. Search keywords updated to match.

rows.title: v1.7.14 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 🛠 EVERY PIECE OF GEAR, HAND-PAINTED — all 41 gear pieces now wear bespoke painterly masters: the rig line grows from a worn pick to a plasma lance, the five suits are true identities on one chassis, four necklaces you can tell apart at a glance, and every Signature relic tells its Beacon’s story. The seven cosmic pieces look like nothing else in the hold — a world being born inside the Genesis Locket, clock hands that disagree about now, a drill bit that is an absence bending light.

rows.title: v1.7.14 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 🚀 THE HULL REMEMBERS EVERY REFIT — the survey-fleet era now marks the ship itself with a gold registry band and navigation strobes, completing the ladder from bare scout to luminous intergalactic craft.

rows.title: v1.7.14 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🤫 DISCOVERIES WAIT THEIR TURN — a new-species reveal no longer pops over an open menu or dialog (it could steal your Escape key); it waits quietly and appears the moment you close what you were doing.

rows.title: v1.7.13 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 🗺 THE STAR CHART — your Atlas gains a second view: every charted place painted across the universe on one deep-space chart, clustered by galaxy, favorites starred, home marked, a quiet crosshair where you stand. Tap any light to travel there. Your filters apply to the chart too.

rows.title: v1.7.13 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 🏷 WORLDS OF RENOWN — the rarest worlds now carry names worth saying twice: “the Shrouded”, “the Ringed Court”, “the Sky Forever”. Rare near home, commoner out in the deep field where legends live. The same world bears the same name for every explorer, forever.

rows.title: v1.7.13 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: ⛏ VEINS WORTH READING — stand on a world and its mineral veins now show their grade for that ground; Primordial worlds enrich every seam one step.

rows.title: v1.7.13 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: ⚔ THE ARENA LEVELED — two fighting styles had quietly drifted stronger than the field (Smite and Roulette); both are back inside the fair band, measured across thousands of simulated duels. Every archetype now wins between 42% and 58% against the field.

rows.title: v1.7.13 ⚖ Balancing
rows.text: 🏆 NO DEAD RELICS — the Graven Aegis and the Prismatic Lathe were weaker than ordinary gear in their own slots; both are now true sidegrades with their own identity (the Aegis holds the protection line with steadier landings; the Lathe trades peak yield for the best rich-strike luck in the game).

rows.title: v1.7.13 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⛏ THE DOUBLE VEIN — metal and lava worlds could list the same mineral twice on their survey card; every vein now appears once.

rows.title: v1.7.12 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🥇 THE PRIMARY SPEAKS SOFTLY — the survey card’s Land button trades its solid gold slab for a gold outline and gold lettering on the shared dark pill. Still unmistakably the next step; no longer shouting over the card.

rows.title: v1.7.11 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: ⛳ THE OBJECTIVE CHIP — the pill under the dock is now a real quest tracker: it always carries the thing you’re doing right now with live progress (“⬆ Mine Sol’s dead worlds · 3 / 8”), pulses when your count moves, follows your accepted charter first and the story chapter otherwise, and opens the board for details.

rows.title: v1.7.11 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 📖 THE MAINLINE READS AS STORY — the chapter pinned atop the Charters board no longer looks like a stack of pre-accepted quests: it wears its own “The Ascent — your mainline” framing with slim progress bars, clearly apart from the optional charters (the ones with Accept buttons) below.

rows.title: v1.7.11 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🗂 THE BINDER MOVES TO RECORDS — type collections, Sets and the Fifty Paragons now live where they belong: a tab on the 🏆 Records board, beside your trophies. The Compendium is purely your living catalogue.

rows.title: v1.7.10 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🔎 SEARCH TAKES THE STAGE — results now drop directly beneath the search box, and everything else falls into shadow while you type, so the answer is the one lit thing on screen.

rows.title: v1.7.10 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🗂 TIDY SHELVES EVERYWHERE — the Compendium and the Shipyard’s Fabricator now open with every shelf and category folded closed; whatever you expand stays expanded for the session. (Training still lays open the shelf a lesson needs.)

rows.title: v1.7.10 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 📖 THE COMPENDIUM CLEARS ITS OWN NAME — the board no longer rides up over the Compendium chip that opened it.

rows.title: v1.7.10 🧭 Gameplay
rows.text: 🎓 LESSONS CLEAR THE STAGE — the feed, breed and heal lessons now put away the specimen card left standing by the previous lesson, so “Open a beast” is true when you read it and the ❤ heart isn’t hiding behind a card.

rows.title: v1.7.10 🧭 Gameplay
rows.text: 🖼 NO DEAD BUTTONS — the Planetside’s ⛶ Full screen pill no longer shows during training, where zoom is deliberately paused so the tap can continue the lesson.

rows.title: v1.7.10 🔧 Under the Hood
rows.text: 🧠 A LIGHTER MEMORY — species lists, search results and roster images now use small thumbnails instead of retaining every full-size portrait; long collecting sessions on phones hold dramatically less memory with no visual change on cards, duels or reveals.

rows.title: v1.7.9 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: ⬆ LEAVE THIS WORLD — every world you’ve stood on now carries an explicit button that pulls the camera back to the system overview. No gesture knowledge required; one press and the whole sky returns.

rows.title: v1.7.9 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🖼 PLANETSIDE ANSWERS INSTANTLY — the landing panorama no longer ignores quick taps (an anti-ghost timer used to eat everything in its first half-second); real taps act immediately, and Escape closes or un-zooms it like everything else.

rows.title: v1.7.9 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: ↺ THE RESET BUTTON KEEPS ITS DISTANCE — a clear gap and quieter styling separate “erase everything” from the harmless Restart-Training row above it. The two-step confirm still stands guard.

rows.title: v1.7.9 ♿ Accessibility
rows.text: 🔇 TRUE MODAL SILENCE — while the Guide, Prime Codex or a duel is up, the world behind the glass is now genuinely unreachable to screen readers and stray taps, and it wakes back up the moment the dialog closes.

rows.title: v1.7.9 ♿ Accessibility
rows.text: 🗒 THE JOURNAL READS ALOUD — the Expedition journal announces itself as a proper list, one landing per row, to assistive technology.

rows.title: v1.7.9 ♿ Accessibility
rows.text: 🏷 NOTIFICATIONS SPEAK WITH ONE VOICE — every notification title now follows the same casing, so nothing reads like it came from a different game.

rows.title: v1.7.8 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🧭 TRAINING STEP 6, UNSTUCK — Earth’s survey card could vanish between the Atlas lesson and the landing lesson with no way to bring it back (opening the Atlas, travelling from its Earth row, or a keyboard Escape could each close it). The card now rides safely into the landing step, tapping Earth always reopens it, and keyboard shortcuts respect the lesson like taps do.

rows.title: v1.7.8 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: ⬆ UPDATES ACTUALLY ARRIVE — the game now checks for a newer build the moment it starts and quietly swaps a stale copy for the live one before play begins (your expedition is untouched — saves live on your device, not in the page). The update pill’s refresh now truly fetches the new build instead of re-serving the cached one.

rows.title: v1.7.7 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: ⌨ THE BOARD ANSWERS THE KEYBOARD — focus the star map and the arrow keys cycle every pickable body nearest-first (a gold dashed ring marks your target), Enter surveys it with full credit, +/− zoom on it, Escape releases. The universe is no longer mouse-only.

rows.title: v1.7.7 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: 🗣 THE GAME SPEAKS — every toast, target change and survey is announced to assistive technology through a live region; boards move focus in when they open and hand it back when they close; Tab stays inside open dialogs; search results walk with ↑/↓ and commit on Enter.

rows.title: v1.7.7 ✦ New Features & Systems
rows.text: ⛳ PLANETFALL CHARTS ITSELF — every world you stand on joins your Star Atlas automatically (the + button stays for orbital bookmarks), and a new ⛳ Visited filter keeps your hand-picked favorites uncrowded. No more losing a world because you forgot to file paperwork.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🛑 A CRASH, CAUGHT — zooming out of a system with a survey card open could throw an error every frame; the card now closes cleanly when its star leaves the view.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🗂 ONE SURFACE AT A TIME — opening any board now puts the survey card away first (boards were stacking on top of it), tapping the card never closes a board, Escape reaches the card too, and on phones the card stops above the dock instead of tangling with it.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🌍 THE WORLD-NAME FIX ACTUALLY SHOWS — the Planetside header’s lowercase landing region was being re-capitalized by styling; “PLANETFALL — MERCURY · carbon world” now reads as intended.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🔔 TOASTS BEHAVE EVERYWHERE — they no longer hide behind the training card (the “expedition saved” note now greets you at graduation), short laptop screens get a left-side lane clear of Records, and tablets show one at a time.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🐛 Bug Fixes
rows.text: 🏷 ONE TITLE PER BOARD — Records and Notifications stopped saying their names twice, and every board now carries its title on desktop as well as phones.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🛠 HONEST SHORTFALLS — an unaffordable recipe lists everything it’s missing (“Need 3× Iron + 1× Chromium”), the buttons can be hovered and tabbed for details, and the Fabricator opens with your closest build and how to close the gap.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 📜 DEEDS ALREADY DONE SAY SO — a charter you’ve already fulfilled shows Claim ✓ instead of asking you to do it again, and accepting it pays on the spot.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🗺 UNDO WHERE YOU NEED IT — removing an Atlas entry offers its undo right in the list, under your finger.

rows.title: v1.7.6 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🔎 SMALL TYPE, RAISED — the rarity ladder, titan guidance lines, dock captions and the control hint (which now wraps instead of cutting off “double-tap zooms”) all stepped up in size or contrast.

rows.title: v1.7.5 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 📏 ROOM TO BREATHE — the control hint pill, the caption above it, and the training card each step cleanly above the dock instead of brushing the chip tops.

rows.title: v1.7.4 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🏷 CAPTIONS THAT GRADUATE — the dock names its boards while you’re in Field Training; complete it and the labels retire, leaving the clean icon dock (they return if you restart training from ⚙ Settings). Prime Codex keeps its count either way.

rows.title: v1.7.3 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 📐 TABLETS GET THEIR OWN HOME — iPads, Surfaces and everything up to 900px now use the dock-and-sheet layout built for touch: boards open as titled, centered sheets above the dock with the world dimmed behind them, instead of desktop furniture squeezed to phone width.

rows.title: v1.7.3 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🏷 THE DOCK SPEAKS — every board chip carries its name under its icon (no more guessing what the scroll means), and every chip, circle and control on touch screens holds the 44px finger floor — Accept buttons, Atlas stars, settings chips included.

rows.title: v1.7.3 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 🖼 BIGGER SKIES — the Planetside vista breathes on tablets, and panels on very large monitors finally grow beyond phone-column width.

rows.title: v1.7.3 🎮 Gameplay
rows.text: 🌀 THE STELLAR SIGNATURE — the Wind Signature is renamed: Zephyrmaw, the Stellar Squall, was always the titan of the solar wind, and now its Signature says so. Air keeps the skies; Stellar takes the stars. Claimed trophies keep their standing — only the name changes.

rows.title: v1.7.2 🖱 UI Enhancements
rows.text: 📜 THE TITANS SPEAK — every Prime Codex titan now tells its own story (Terrakoth stands where the crust runs richest; Sylphrend rides the cloud decks…), the guidance lines wrap instead of cutting mid-word, and locked rows read clearly.

rows.title: v1.7.2 🖱 UI Enhancements
